summary: This Makefile snippet defines a phony target called 'current_dir' that, when invoked, prints out the current working directory. The PWD variable is set at the beginning using a shell command to capture the actual directory path.

explanations.1: PWD:=$(shell pwd) runs the 'pwd' command (which prints the working directory) and stores the result in a variable named PWD that can be used later with ${PWD}.
explanations.3: current_dir: is a target name—when you run 'make current_dir', this is what gets executed.
explanations.4: The @ symbol before echo suppresses printing the echo command itself, so you only see the output message, not the command. ${PWD} substitutes in the directory path we captured earlier.
